step.name: Deploy manager QDMA customization
step.description: Override XilinxAlveoV80InstanceDeployManager to use QDMA instead of XDMA. The parent class XilinxAlveoInstanceDeployManager calls load_xdma() (XDMA kernel module), flash_fpgas() (programs .bit files via Vivado), and assumes XDMA device files. V80 needs: (1) load_qdma() — load qdma-pf kernel module, set qmax, add/start MM queues via dma-ctl; (2) flash_fpgas() — program .pdi files (Versal uses PDI, not .bit) via vivado -mode batch with program_hw_devices; (3) PCIe re-enumeration after PDI programming (Versal full-bitstream drops PCIe link). Reference the CorigineXB10InstanceDeployManager for the pattern of overriding create_fpga_database(). Reference the driver code (simif_xilinx_alveo_v80.cc) for QDMA device naming convention (/dev/qdmaXXXXX-MM-0).
success_criteria: XilinxAlveoV80InstanceDeployManager overrides load_xdma with QDMA-specific logic (module load, queue setup)
flash_fpgas() method programs PDI files instead of .bit files
PCIe re-enumeration or recovery is handled after PDI programming
QDMA queue setup matches what the driver expects (MM queue 0, bidirectional)
Python code passes basic linting/import checks

parts.description: Create V80 deploy scripts directory by copying shared platform scripts from xilinx_alveo_u250. These scripts handle PCIe disconnect/reconnect (firesim-fpga-util.py, pcielib.py), JTAG programming (program_fpga_fleet.tcl, program_fpga.tcl), FPGA DB generation (firesim-generate-fpga-db.py), and Vivado helpers (util.py). The program_fpga_fleet.tcl already supports PDI files via program_hw_devices. Copy all files from $FIRESIM/platforms/xilinx_alveo_u250/scripts/ to $FIRESIM/platforms/xilinx_alveo_v80/scripts/, preserving executable permissions. Files to copy: pcielib.py, util.py, firesim-fpga-util.py, firesim-generate-fpga-db.py, program_fpga_fleet.tcl, get_serial_dev_for_fpgas.tcl, program_fpga.tcl, program_fpga_all.tcl, program_flash.tcl, berkeley-setup-fpgas.sh. $FIRESIM is /home/ray/chipyard/sims/firesim.
parts.done_when: Directory $FIRESIM/platforms/xilinx_alveo_v80/scripts/ exists with all 10 scripts matching the U250 scripts directory listing. Executable scripts (firesim-fpga-util.py, firesim-generate-fpga-db.py, berkeley-setup-fpgas.sh) retain execute permission.

parts.description:
Add QDMA load/unload methods and flash_fpgas override to XilinxAlveoV80InstanceDeployManager in $FIRESIM/deploy/runtools/run_farm_deploy_managers.py. Three methods to add:

(A) load_qdma(self): If instance has assigned simulations: (1) Load qdma-pf kernel module if not loaded (check via 'lsmod | grep -wq qdma_pf'), using 'sudo modprobe qdma-pf' or the equivalent script. (2) For each FPGA slot, get the BDF from the FPGA DB, compute the QDMA BDF encoding as (bus<<12)|(device<<4)|function (matching the driver's simif_xilinx_alveo_v80.cc convention), set qmax via 'echo 512 > /sys/bus/pci/devices/0000:{bdf}/qdma/qmax', then run 'dma-ctl qdma{qdma_bdf:05x} q add idx 0 mode mm dir bi' and 'dma-ctl qdma{qdma_bdf:05x} q start idx 0 dir bi'. (3) chmod 666 /dev/qdma* for permissions.

(B) unload_qdma(self): If instance has assigned simulations and qdma_pf is loaded: For each FPGA slot, compute QDMA BDF and run 'dma-ctl qdma{qdma_bdf:05x} q stop idx 0 dir bi' and 'dma-ctl qdma{qdma_bdf:05x} q del idx 0 dir bi' (warn_only since queues might not exist). Then 'sudo modprobe -r qdma-pf'.

(C) flash_fpgas(self): Override the base class method. The V80 build already copies PDI as firesim.bit in post_impl.tcl, so the bitstream unpacking/naming is the same. The key V80 difference is PCIe re-enumeration after PDI programming: Versal full-bitstream PDI programming resets the SoC and drops the PCIe link. Flow: (1) PCI disconnect all slots (same as base class, using firesim-fpga-util.py --disconnect-bdf). (2) Program all FPGAs via Vivado batch with program_fpga_fleet.tcl (same as base class). (3) After programming, wait for PCIe link to re-establish (sleep 5-10 seconds for Versal link training). (4) Do a full PCIe bus rescan via 'echo 1 > /sys/bus/pci/rescan' (sudo). (5) Retry rescan up to 30 seconds if devices don't appear. (6) Enable memory-mapped transfers on reappeared devices (setpci -s EBDF COMMAND=0x02). Do NOT call the base class's per-BDF reconnect since the BDF may change after Versal reprogramming; use full bus rescan instead.

Helper: Add a _compute_qdma_bdf(self, bdf_str) method that takes a BDF string like 'b1:00.0', splits it, and returns the integer (bus<<12)|(device<<4)|function. This matches the driver convention in simif_xilinx_alveo_v80.cc.

$FIRESIM is /home/ray/chipyard/sims/firesim. The class starts at line 1447. Use fabric's run() for remote commands. Reference the base class at line 1047 for the pattern. Use warn_only=True for operations that might fail gracefully (queue teardown).
parts.build_command: python3 -c "import ast; ast.parse(open('/home/ray/chipyard/sims/firesim/deploy/runtools/run_farm_deploy_managers.py').read()); print('AST parse OK')" && python3 -c "import ast; tree = ast.parse(open('/home/ray/chipyard/sims/firesim/deploy/runtools/run_farm_deploy_managers.py').read()); cls = [n for n in ast.walk(tree) if isinstance(n, ast.ClassDef) and n.name == 'XilinxAlveoV80InstanceDeployManager'][0]; methods = [n.name for n in cls.body if isinstance(n, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef))]; assert 'load_qdma' in methods, f'load_qdma missing, got {methods}'; assert 'unload_qdma' in methods, f'unload_qdma missing'; assert 'flash_fpgas' in methods, f'flash_fpgas missing'; print(f'V80 methods: {methods}')"
parts.done_when: XilinxAlveoV80InstanceDeployManager class has load_qdma(), unload_qdma(), flash_fpgas(), and _compute_qdma_bdf() methods. Python AST parse succeeds. load_qdma loads qdma-pf module, sets qmax, adds MM queue 0 bidirectional, starts it. unload_qdma tears down queues and removes module. flash_fpgas programs PDI via Vivado and handles PCIe re-enumeration with full bus rescan and retry. The QDMA BDF encoding matches the driver: (bus<<12)|(device<<4)|function formatted as 5-digit hex.

parts.description:
Add lifecycle override methods to XilinxAlveoV80InstanceDeployManager in $FIRESIM/deploy/runtools/run_farm_deploy_managers.py. Four methods to add/override:

(A) infrasetup_instance(self, uridir): Override the base class method (line 1211 of base). Copy the base class logic but replace self.unload_xdma() with self.unload_qdma(), self.load_xdma() with self.load_qdma(). Keep copy_sim_slot_infrastructure, extract_driver_tarball, flash_fpgas (which is already overridden in Part 2), change_pcie_perms, and switch/pipe slot copying as-is. The flow is: copy sim infrastructure -> if not metasim: unload_qdma -> flash_fpgas -> load_qdma -> change_pcie_perms.

(B) enumerate_fpgas(self, uridir): Override the base class method (line 1290). Copy the base class logic but replace self.unload_xdma() with self.unload_qdma() and self.load_xdma() with self.load_qdma(). Keep change_all_pcie_perms and create_fpga_database as-is.

(C) start_sim_slot(self, slotno): Override the base class method (line 1309). Copy the base class logic but change the extra_args to pass +bar=0x1 instead of +bar=0x0 (V80 uses BAR1 for MMIO, as defined in simif_xilinx_alveo_v80.cc: 'uint32_t bar1_size = 0x2000000; // 32 MB BAR1'). Keep the rest identical: +domain, +bus, +device, +function, +pci-vendor=0x10ee, +pci-device=0x903f.

(D) create_fpga_database(self, uridir): Override following the CorigineXB10 pattern (line 1379). The method should be nearly identical to CorigineXB10's create_fpga_database (which is itself nearly identical to the base class but uses a single-session Vivado approach). The V80 version should use self.PLATFORM_NAME ('xilinx_alveo_v80') and reference the correct driver binary name 'FireSim-xilinx_alveo_v80'. Use the standard firesim-generate-fpga-db.py script (not v2) — same as base class. The key difference from the base class is the single-session approach that avoids the hw_server wedge.

$FIRESIM is /home/ray/chipyard/sims/firesim. The class is XilinxAlveoV80InstanceDeployManager. Reference the base class methods starting at line 1047 for the patterns to copy and modify.

Python AST parse succeeds. infrasetup_instance and enumerate_fpgas call load_qdma/unload_qdma (not load_xdma/unload_xdma). start_sim_slot passes +bar=0x1. create_fpga_database follows the CorigineXB10 single-session pattern with PLATFORM_NAME='xilinx_alveo_v80'.

parts.description:
Dry-run verification of deploy manager QDMA code. This part validates that the deploy manager Python code written in Parts 2-3 is functionally correct beyond just AST parsing, and cross-checks consistency between the C++ driver (simif_xilinx_alveo_v80.cc) and the deploy manager Python code. Four verifications:

(A) Import and instantiation test: Write a test script at $FIRESIM/deploy/tests/test_v80_deploy_manager.py that imports XilinxAlveoV80InstanceDeployManager, verifies it can be referenced without import errors, and checks that all expected methods exist with correct signatures (using inspect.signature). This runs inside the container where the FireSim Python environment is available.

(B) QDMA BDF encoding unit test: Test _compute_qdma_bdf() with known inputs. BDF 'b1:00.0' should produce (0xb1 << 12) | (0x00 << 4) | 0x0 = 0xb1000 = 724992. BDF '3b:00.0' should produce (0x3b << 12) | (0x00 << 4) | 0x0 = 0x3b000 = 241664. BDF '86:00.1' should produce (0x86 << 12) | (0x00 << 4) | 0x1 = 0x86001. Verify the 5-digit hex formatting: f'{qdma_bdf:05x}' produces 'b1000', '3b000', '86001' respectively. These must match the device names the driver expects (/dev/qdmaXXXXX-MM-0).

(C) Command sequence audit: Review the shell commands generated by load_qdma(), unload_qdma(), and flash_fpgas() by inspecting the source code. Verify: (1) load_qdma sets qmax BEFORE adding queues (required by QDMA driver — adding a queue before setting qmax fails). (2) load_qdma adds queue with 'mode mm dir bi' (not 'mode st' — FireSim uses memory-mapped, not streaming). (3) flash_fpgas does PCIe rescan AFTER programming (not before). (4) unload_qdma stops queues BEFORE deleting them. (5) The modprobe commands use 'qdma-pf' (hyphen, the module alias) not 'qdma_pf' (underscore, the internal name) — both work with modprobe but dma-ctl uses the hyphen convention.

(D) C++ driver / deploy manager cross-check: Read $FIRESIM/sim/midas/src/main/cc/simif_xilinx_alveo_v80.cc and verify consistency with the deploy manager code. Specifically: (1) The QDMA BDF encoding in the C++ driver (how it constructs the /dev/qdmaXXXXX-MM-0 device path from BDF) uses the same (bus<<12)|(dev<<4)|func formula as _compute_qdma_bdf(). Extract the C++ code that builds the device path string and confirm the encoding matches. (2) The C++ driver's BAR index for MMIO (bar1_size variable, BAR1 = index 1) matches the +bar=0x1 argument in start_sim_slot(). (3) The C++ driver's expected BAR size (0x2000000 = 32 MB for BAR1) is consistent with the Scala config CtrlNastiKey addrBits=25 (2^25 = 32 MB). (4) The C++ driver's DMA device file pattern (/dev/qdma{bdf}-MM-0) matches the queue setup in load_qdma() (mode mm, idx 0, dir bi). (5) The C++ driver's PCI vendor/device IDs (0x10ee/0x903f) match the +pci-vendor and +pci-device args in start_sim_slot(). Add these cross-checks to the test script with clear pass/fail output. If any mismatch is found, report it as a test failure with both the C++ and Python values.

$FIRESIM is /home/ray/chipyard/sims/firesim.
parts.done_when: test_v80_deploy_manager.py exists and passes all four verification categories. _compute_qdma_bdf returns correct values for at least 3 test BDFs. All expected methods exist on XilinxAlveoV80InstanceDeployManager. Command sequence audit confirms correct ordering. C++ driver cross-check confirms: BDF encoding matches, BAR index is 1, BAR size is 32 MB, device file pattern matches queue setup, PCI IDs match.
